title: The user needs to have document citations for relevant passages not for the full document only.
The user needs custom, savable agents ("Gems") for recurring tasks.
The user needs configurable citation length — shorter inline citations while keeping full-length citations available elsewhere.
The user needs to be able to create and use templates in multiple languages without creating a template per language.
The user needs to be able to collapse or minimize the question box so answers get more screen space.
The user needs to be able to create templates for Matrix Analysis.
The user needs to be able to duplicate an existing Matrix Analysis.
The (non-admin) user needs to be able to create private templates for themselves.
The user needs Swiss court decisions to be chunked and cited at the "Erwägung" level rather than by fixed size, matching the court's own reasoning structure.
The user needs to be able to resize Matrix Analysis column widths.
The user needs to be able to duplicate existing templates for reuse in similar use cases with slight variations.
The user needs conditional formatting (e.g. colour, bold, flags) in Matrix Analysis cells, triggered by prompt results.
The user-input feature should allow both text and file input, not either/or.
The user needs to be able to accept only a selected part of a proposed clause/suggestion into the document, rather than the whole suggestion.
The user needs a copy button in the Editor, like the one available in the chat.
The user needs comments/annotations placed directly at the relevant location in the document, with a settable commenter name and clearer colour coding, for direct hand-off into Word.
The users need to be able to work on their mobile phone, e.g. through an iOS app.
Users want in-product support — a phone line or live chat directly in the interface.
The users need generated output delivered as a downloadable PPTX file.
The user needs edits on one side of a two-column bilingual document to propagate automatically to the other side across the entire document.
Users want to reference documents inline in the editor via @ mentions, and reference existing chats via @ to pull documents and results from them.
Users want template generation that consolidates overlaps across similar documents and surfaces differences as optional text blocks.
Users want configurable citation style; the default citation format is unusual in German legal scholarship and practice.
The user needs access to answers from previous sessions in order to maintain continuity across chats.
The user needs inline AI clause suggestions directly in Word while drafting a contract.
The user needs the tool to automate routine administrative steps (e.g. dispatching decrees to attorneys whose addresses are already known).
The user needs the tool to conduct autonomous research and tool calls, rather than requiring the user to provide context manually.
The user needs the tool to verify and correctly link cited rulings and sources within incoming submissions from parties.
The user needs the tool to flag contradictions between submissions and suggest fact-finding gaps for offence elements.
The user needs the tool to keep track of what has already been read or written in a long-running case, so they do not duplicate work.
The user needs the tool to support cross-border procedural comparison (e.g. covert seizure in Austria) for trans-national cases.
The user needs the tool to automatically extract procedural data (admissibility, deadlines, time limits) from case files.
The user needs the tool to automatically suggest relevant case law and judgments in the background when a case file is opened.
The user needs the vendor to proactively curate and maintain templates and checklists within the tool over time.
The user needs unlimited input and output length for template-filling tasks.
The user needs the tool to cover EU regulations and EU case law alongside national law in one unified tool.
The user needs the tool to optimise their English drafting on demand into proper legal English.
The user needs the tool to extract and present a tabular overview of contractual obligations, rights, and termination notice periods from a contract.
The user needs the tool to generate visual diagrams (Schaubilder) of contractual relationships from large contracts.
The user needs the tool to flag cross-clause and cross-domain impacts (e.g. tax, antitrust) automatically when one clause is changed.
The user needs the tool to redline an existing Word document with minimal changes rather than regenerating a new document from scratch.
The user needs motivational features (e.g. streaks, daily nudges) to encourage consistent tool use.
The user needs the tool to automatically keep requesters informed of the progress of their request.
The user needs the tool to balance workload across team members based on current capacity.
The user needs the tool to accept and consolidate requests from multiple input channels (email, intranet form, voice/phone) into one unified system.
The user needs AI self-service surfaces per business unit so non-legal users can self-serve, with legal teams curating the knowledge base and human-in-the-loop escalation available when needed.
The user needs the tool to automatically detect deadlines and urgency from incoming items and proactively create calendar entries, tasks, and reminders.
The user needs to have cantonal jurisprudence and laws integrated into the database.
The user needs the Word-Add-In to be able to work with footnotes in order to have sources less prominent in the document.
The user would like to be able to comment on matrixes in order to communicate with team members or other parties.
The user needs clear transparency on existing limitations, e.g. upload limitations.

The user needs to be able to differentiate fine granularly what other users can do to templates/ workflows (i.e. creating, using, modifying, and deleting them), in order to have control over quality and access.
The user needs the tool to automatically generate documents pre-populated with employee names in the Editor.
The user needs to be able to upload documents from DATEV DMS directly without encountering file format errors.
The user needs the settings to be easily discoverable in order to configure the tool to their needs.

The user needs to be able to restrict certain features (such as file or outlook integration) for certain user groups, that work on highly confidential topics or are too junior to judge what can be shared.
The user would like to enable clients to take over parts of their work supported by AI, so that they are more the reviewing and strategic instance.
The user wants the AI to automatically update the information in the knowledge base based on changes in the law or commentaries.
The user needs to be able to share files in the knowledge base with ceratin teams.
The user needs to be able to export the final result that a workflow produced for documentation/ sharing purposes.
The user would like to get suggestions for new workflows based on his usage of the AI.
The user would like to be able to tell the tool how harsh or lenient the AI should be when reviewing and suggesting changes to a document.
The user needs to be able to get an overview of all changes to evaluate them in context, to be able to make a decision on each of the changes.
The user needs clear guidance options for controlled AI deployment, similar to a data room approach.
The user needs a prompt library as a central working resource.
The user would like to be able to work in another chat while the prompt is running.
The user wants the system to automatically update matrices with new decisions.
The user expects the tool to be able to translate legal findings into technical/product implications, in order to communicate them efficiently to other (non-legal) parties.
The user wants to be able to share generated matrixes with their colleagues.
The user needs to be able to give feedback regarding the quality of the task fulfillment.

The user needs transparency on how to add user input to a template.
The user needs an option to prevent accidental message submission when pressing Enter.
The user needs a single, unambiguous login entry point instead of two confusing options (publisher portal vs. direct app link).
The user needs voice input for long transcription of dictated text or meetings.
The user needs an "Artefakte" section that surfaces uploaded documents alongside citations, and eventually the playbook used.
The user expects the tool to adhere to his instructions (e.g. limitations to sources of interest).
The user needs the tool to not be influenced by an arguing user unless the tool actually uncovers new information in the system, that changes the result.
Marginal numbers (Randziffern) in responses are often too long to be usable.
Date/deadline calculations are almost always wrong when reference dates are entered (weekdays, week-based deadlines).
RVG and court-cost calculations are wildly wrong — amounts are not correctly taken from the tables.
Required user input is not visible when applying a template — the user must click 'edit' to see it.
User-input instructions are not displayed for file inputs, even when essential.
The users find it unclear during template creation whether defining and referencing user inputs is mandatory or optional, and whether it improves output.
The template description character limit is not communicated at creation, so users write text that gets truncated.
The template description should be optional — when mandatory, users just paste prompt fragments.
The template naming field should be more prominent.
The user wants underlying sources inserted as clickable links (not only footnotes) directly in the document.
The user finds the pricing too high for solo practitioners / small firms and would like a more economical offer.
The user needs to be able to fully clear or delete the Editor content in one action, instead of the tool overwriting, appending to, or being unable to rebuild it.
The user expects for pleadings/briefs that the structure is met, currently its often missing required legal formalities (e.g. Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung, Anrede, Grußformel).
Users would like memory / learning across sessions, and want the tool to engage with counter-arguments when they present a differing result.
The user expects a faster response / generation speed at the moment its rated as too slow.
The user needs Matrix Analysis Excel exports to include the column prompts on a separate sheet for documentation purposes.
The users need the tool to produce prose-based, running-text output by default and avoid excessive use of bullet points.
The user needs copied text to preserve citation references correctly, without leaving stray spaces behind.
The user needs the tool to help decode unfamiliar business-unit jargon so they can quickly understand what a case is about.
The user expects prior question's context to be taken into account for follow-up questions(e.g. the previously named statute).
The user expects a source to only be listed once in a paragraph to improve readability.
The user needs an indicator of how current/outdated the content is, e.g. showing the document date directly with each source
The user needs the Thinking Process to always be displayed in the language of the prompt.
The user expects the thinking process to work with human-readable labels instead of surfacing technical terms in order to understand it more easily.
The user expects the preview to be optimzed for reading even when there are many footnotes in the source.
The user needs the tool to practice multilingual source matching: French-language questions should also surface German/Italian/English references (and reverse).
The user needs Matrix Analysis prompts to be preserved when re-opening "Spalte bearbeiten".
The user needs multi-step reasoning to be maintained consistently across more than 5 conversation turns.
Users cannot clearly tell whether the system is still processing or has already finished, due to missing or unclear progress indicators.
The user needs the last engaged chat to be at the top, not the last newly created one.
The user needs the login to be smooth an easy and ideally not happen too often.
The user needs the tool to automatically select the right way of working (i.e. selecting the right templates or features) in order to avoid having to do it manually.
The user needs the editor to save all made changes, when they change to another chat to avoid data loss.
The user wishes the export of the matrix to keep the well-structured overview.
The user needs the chat overview to include when the chat happened.
The user needs the snippets of the citations to give them all context needed.
The user needs the tool to use smaller headlines for better readability of the export.
The user needs the sources to be linked (clickable) in the export and not only in the chat.
The user needs to be able to mark a section in the chat and prompt referring to this section in order to work more efficiently.
The user expects the tool to not be biased by context that is given in a chat beforehand to stay objective.
The user needs a clearer structure of the sources overview in order to be able to work with it.
The user wants the chat to be structured like legal case files, in order to fit their usual structures.
The user expects the chat to display the correct date at all times.
The user would like to have some guidance on how much information they need to provide to set up a workflow (step).
The user would like to be able to set company specific elements for workflows that can be shared and reused.
The user would like to be supported in identifying who else needs to be involved in a specific case in a workflow to give them access to the case.
The user would like to be supported in prioritzing currently running workflows (and their results) to be able to know which one to focus on first.
The user needs the producers of the AI to commit to ethical training of the AI to avoid bias and offer the option to notify them if a bias is encountered.
The user needs the tool to be approved by the "Anwältekammer" in order to be able to trust it with confidential information.
The user needs the tool to support using gender neutral/ inclusive speech or at least give me the opportunity to enable it.
The user needs a quick overview of what the tool can and can not do, in order to start working with it and learning on the go.
The user needs the tool to monitor sources (newsletters, databases etc.) and provide me with an overview of recent changes and what they imply regularly.
The user needs the AI to help me find uncertainties or potential errors by evaluating its own performance/ certainty.
The user needs a digital "Schmierzettel" in order to organize my thoughts and findings to put it together later.
The user wants to be able to seleting whole folders for usage in a prompt in order to not have select all documents manually.

The user needs the knowledge base and especially editing and uploading of documents to be retricted in order to make sure information is correct and not everybody can change documents or upload them publicly without review.
The user wants to be able to ask questions to documents within their knowledge base in order to identify the answer.
The user wants to be able to add tags in the knowledge base to improve filtering and searchability.
The user wants to be able to provide access to workflows not only for individual workflows but also by workflow groups, that they can set up .
The user would like to be able to also run parts of workflows only.
The user would like to be able to adjust an existing workflow based on their needs (e.g. changing parameters).
The user would like to be actively involved if multiple options to proceed arise.
The user would like to stay in control and decide whether they want suggestions for workflow improvements from the AI or not.
The user would like the AI to suggest next logical steps based on the already existing ones in a workflow.
The user would like to predefine in the workflow which specific parts of a template should be adjusted/ filled based on the input.
The user would like to be able to create/ adjust a workflow using drag & drop to make it es effortless as possible.
The user would like to be able to define triggers, which would lead to starting the workflow.
The user needs a dashboard or a whiteboard on which I can insert single prompts which all can be integrated into one workflow.
The user would like to be able to improve an existing workflow in cooperation with noxtua by active prompting.
The user wants to be able to add prompts to a tool case which they can reuse or adjust to their needs.
The user need the document drafting to be more detailed in order to be able to continue working with the generated document.
The user wants to know which file is affected if one of the files can't be read.
The user needs the tool to support visual language (VL) capabilities so that floor plans can be used for rental agreement tasks.
The user needs to not be limited by context window size constraints when working with large documents or complex tasks. (Proposed solution: option to set context window to 250,000 tokens or higher.)
The user needs references in pleadings or contracts to be more strongly and reliably linked.
The user would like to be able to create slide and speaker bulletpoints for a specific topic to transfer that to powerpoint for speeches.
The user needs the system to indicate legal uncertainty if there are alternative viewpoints or if there are ongoing debates.
The users need to be able to easily understand the research output.
The user needs the system to be more resistant to upper and lower case writing.
The users want to be able to select only parts of the answer to copy for further usage, e.g. excluding thinking or certain detailed explanations.
The user does not want to see citations that are not wrong, but granted in order to avoid having too many sources.
The user needs the tool to provide accurate answers on the first attempt, without requiring multiple follow-up queries to reach the correct solution.
User need to get all relevant sources linked to their answer in order to get the full picture.
The user needs direct links to Beck-Online sources to be included in the output.
The users don't want the citation panel to pop-up automatically, particularly when Editor is open.
The users find the presence of change buttons before any edits were made confusing.
The user wants the tool to highlight significant changes to them in order to easier navigate especially big edits that the tool makes to documents.
The user expects the tool to offer both structured (decision-tree-like) and flexible (more creative) editing of documents to accommodate both standard but also exceptional cases.
Users want to replace prompting by filling Dropdowns in order to avoid having to write prompts.
The users expect the tool to stick to the language of an uploaded document and not to e.g. switch to German just because the prompt was German.
The users would like to see the content mapped to specific pages, i.e. page breaks and page numbering.
Users want to be able to mark up (color highlights) documents for clarity and emphasis.
User want to be able to insert line breaks in prompts easily with one click.
The user needs Matrix Analysis to apply consistent logic between columns and across rows.
The user needs Matrix Analysis results to be reliable and expects the tool to handle law updates clearly, without requiring manual review.
The user needs to be able to compare different legislations easily.
The user doesn't want to see the interim results but only the final result.
The user expects the answer to be updated with the information from follow-up prompting instead of just appending it at the end.
The user needs a general workflow to check the different types of documents.
The user wants to be supported in taking the right measures to a request.
The user would like to be able to integrate their thoughts with the official information from the provided sources.
The user needs the tool to chose the sources based on the nature of the question. E.g. Formularhandbücher used as a substitute source: unsuitable for doctrinal questions.
The user needs also information for very specific topics to be available so that he can use the tool for their tasks.
